The ""new"" fragmentation code (since my rewrite almost 5 years ago)
erroneously sets skb->len rather than using skb_trim() to adjust
the length of the first fragment after copying out all the others.
This leaves the skb tail pointer pointing to after where the data
originally ended
column2: and thus causes the encryption MIC to be written

column1: at that point
column2: rather than where it belongs: immediately after the

column1: data.
The impact of this is that if software encryption is done
a) encryption doesn't work for the first fragment
becomes unusable as the first fragment will never be properly
verified at the receiver
column2: the MIC is practically guaranteed to

column1: be wrong
b) we leak up to 8 bytes of plaintext (!) of the packet out into
the air
This is only mitigated by the fact that many devices are capable
of doing encryption in hardware
column2: in which case this can't happen

column1: as the tail pointer is irrelevant in that case. Additionally
fragmentation is not used very frequently and would normally have
to be configured manually.
Fix this by using skb_trim() properly.
